nodes.text: It is said that Glum dreamed one night. He seemed
to be standing outside on his farm, looking out toward the fjord.
He seemed to see a woman walking up through the district from the coast,
and she was heading here to Thvera. And she was so
huge that her shoulders touched the mountains on both
sides. And he seemed to go out of the yard to meet her and
invited her to his home. And then he woke. Everyone thought it strange,
but he says this: The dream is great and remarkable,
but I will read it this way: that Vigfus, my mother's
father, must now be dead. And that woman must
be his *hamingja* [guardian spirit of luck], who walked higher than the mountains. And he was beyond
other men in most things in honour. And his luck
will seek a home there, where I am.
And in the summer, when ships came out, the death
of Vigfus was reported. Then Glum spoke a verse: I saw go, under a helmet, of the hawk's islet
